title: Cluster brief mini-slate and burst policy editor
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact 'cluster brief' mini-slate that surfaces GPU pool health, short-term capacity headroom, and a lightweight burst-policy editor for ops users. The mini-slate will live as a card in the Dedicated Capacity overview and as a collapsed flyout from pool rows. The goal is to let SREs and platform engineers quickly assess risk and apply conservative burst/rollback policies without leaving the console.
acceptance_criteria: Mini-slate shows: pool CPU/GPU utilization sparkline, tokenized latency P95, remaining reserved headroom (vCPU/GPU), and simple cost delta estimate for a 1-hour burst
Burst policy editor supports: instant burst toggle, tiered burst windows (1/10/60 min), hysteresis slider (sensitivity), and a 'graceful rollback' option
Editor changes can be previewed with estimated unit-cost impact and are saveable as named presets
Mini-slate accessible from pool list row via 'peek' flyout and as persistent card in cluster overview; both respect RBAC (no editor if view-only)
Design has annotated responsive states for narrow consoles (<=1000px) and dark theme variations
Prototype flows validated in two usability sessions with SRE and Platform PM and updated after feedback
notes: Rationale: many ops incidents begin with lack of visibility into short-term headroom—current console UX requires drilling into pool detail to make a policy change. The mini-slate reduces context switching.

Trade-offs: to preserve cognitive simplicity we limit editor to conservative knobs (tiered windows + hysteresis) rather than full autoscale rule authoring. Full rule authoring remains in Fleet settings.
Data constraints: cost delta is an estimate derived from recent per-token cost and active job mix; backend will need a server-side endpoint for 'burst_cost_estimate' (Engineering dependency).
Privacy/Security: editor respects role-level permissions; preview uses anonymized workload samples when shown to non-owner users.
